name: Sumprat
classification_notes: An experimental display typeface with two named stylistic variants – Grate and Wire – suggesting contrasting textural or structural treatments of the letterforms. Consistent with Daytona Mess's broader practice of designing at the boundary between legibility and illegibility.
summary: A free experimental display typeface in two contrasting variants, Grate and Wire, from Paris-based designer Anne-Dauphine Borione.
description: Sumprat comes in two stylistic variants – Grate and Wire – whose names point to contrasting structural treatments: one constructed from grid-like or barred forms, the other from thin wire-like strokes. The typeface includes case-sensitive OpenType forms and size-based features, suggesting some typographic consideration beneath the experimental surface. Suited to highly specific editorial or poster contexts where an unconventional letterform is the point.
foundry_blurb: Part of Daytona Mess's experimental type world, Sumprat is released free for commercial use under the Open Font Licence, available directly via the designer's fonts.xyz storefront.
